candidates.description: Rewrite the allocation query to compute the running remaining balance in the database using a correlated sub‑query and return a `PaymentHistoryLineDto` directly. This eliminates the intermediate `InvoiceAllocationRowDto` and the per‑row arithmetic loop, cutting the number of object allocations per result row from two to one while preserving the exact response content.
candidates.predicted_effect: allocations per request drop from 2 × N (InvoiceAllocationRowDto + PaymentHistoryLineDto) to 1 × N (only PaymentHistoryLineDto)
candidates.sql_before: select new com.ex.dto.InvoiceAllocationRowDto(i.amount, i.status, pa.id, p.paidOn, pa.allocatedAmount, p.method) from Invoice i left join PaymentAllocation pa on pa.invoiceId = i.id left join CustomerPayment p on p.id = pa.paymentId where i.id = :invoiceId order by p.paidOn asc, p.id asc, pa.id asc
candidates.sql_after: select new com.ex.dto.PaymentHistoryLineDto(pa.id, p.paidOn, pa.allocatedAmount, p.method, i.amount - (select coalesce(sum(pa2.allocatedAmount),0) from PaymentAllocation pa2 where pa2.invoiceId = i.id and (pa2.paidOn < p.paidOn or (pa2.paidOn = p.paidOn and pa2.id <= pa.id))) from Invoice i left join PaymentAllocation pa on pa.invoiceId = i.id left join CustomerPayment p on p.id = pa.paymentId where i.id = :invoiceId order by p.paidOn asc, p.id asc, pa.id asc
what_could_break: The JPQL sub‑query may produce different ordering semantics if the database optimizer rewrites it; extensive testing is required.
If the correlated sub‑query is not supported by the JPA provider, a native query would be needed, which could affect portability.
